neighbours.label: crop-processing words (plantation, roasting, harvest) when the crop is tea, coffee or cocoa; the same words for wheat, peanuts or meat stay low
fire: In Kenya the tea plantations stretch across the highlands for miles.
Small batch roasting brings out the fruity notes in Ethiopian coffee.
Workers on the coffee plantation pick the ripe cherries by hand.
After the cocoa harvest, the beans are fermented under banana leaves.
Darjeeling growers wait for the first flush harvest of tea each spring.
Light roasting keeps more of the acidity in the coffee beans.
Many cocoa plantations in Ivory Coast rely on family labour.
The estate runs tours of its tea plantation and drying sheds.
quiet: In Kansas the wheat fields stretch across the plains for miles.
Slow roasting brings out the sweetness in a leg of lamb.
Workers on the cotton farm pick the ripe bolls by hand.
After the grape harvest, the juice is fermented in steel tanks.
Potato growers wait for the first harvest of new potatoes each spring.
Light toasting keeps more of the crunch in the almonds.
Many rubber farms in Malaysia rely on family labour.
The estate runs tours of its apple orchard and cider sheds.
